title: Dodecanuclear [MnIII6LnIII6] species: synthesis, structures and characterization of magnetic relaxation phenomena

material_class.structural_family: dodecanuclear Mn6Gd6 cluster with central cubane-like and defective-cubane units

synthesis.procedure: The reaction of Mn(O2CPh)2·2H2O, Gd(NO3)3·6H2O and H3L (2-(β-naphthalideneamino)-2-hydroxymethyl-1-propanol) in a 1:1:1 ratio in the presence of NEt3 afforded [Mn6IIIGd6III(OH)7(H2O)3(O2CPh)11(L)3(HL)4(NO3)]·6.5MeCN·H2O. No solvent, temperature, time, work-up or yield is given in the main text.
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Single crystals of 1 were obtained and used for X-ray crystallography; crystallization conditions are not stated in the main text.

properties.summary: DC susceptibility (0.1 T, 5–300 K) gives room-temperature χMT = 66.65 cm3 K mol−1, close to the spin-only value of 65.25 cm3 K mol−1 for six MnIII (g = 2.0) and six GdIII (g = 2.00). χMT rises slightly on cooling and reaches 76.81 cm3 K mol−1 at 5 K, attributed mainly to MnIII–GdIII and GdIII–GdIII interactions. Variable-temperature/field magnetization (about 2–7 K, 0.5–7 T as printed) could not be fitted to an isolated ground state. No out-of-phase ac signal is observed.

material_class.structural_family: dodecanuclear Mn6Dy6 cluster proposed isostructural with the Gd analogue

synthesis.procedure: The reaction of Mn(O2CPh)2·2H2O, Dy(NO3)3·6H2O and H3L (2-(β-naphthalideneamino)-2-hydroxymethyl-1-propanol) in a 1:1:1 ratio in the presence of NEt3 afforded [Mn6IIIDy6III(OH)7(H2O)3(O2CPh)11(L)3(HL)4(NO3)]·6.5MeCN·H2O. No solvent, temperature, time, work-up or yield is given in the main text.

properties.summary: DC susceptibility (0.1 T, 5–300 K) gives room-temperature χMT = 96.72 cm3 K mol−1, slightly below 102.57 cm3 K mol−1 expected for six MnIII (g = 2.0) and six DyIII (S = 5/2, L = 5, J = 15/2, gJ = 4/3). χMT is nearly constant to about 100 K, then falls to 62.38 cm3 K mol−1 at 5 K. Ac susceptibility shows frequency-dependent, almost fully formed out-of-phase signals below roughly the low-temperature regime cited in the text, consistent with possible SMM behaviour; the in-phase signal decreases on cooling, indicating low-lying excited states.
